dialect.detail: GnuCOBOL (OpenCOBOL) - uses COB_SCREEN_EXCEPTIONS, COB_SCREEN_ESC, COB_EXIT_WAIT environment variables, COB-SCR-F12, COB-SCR-ESC screen status constants, and cob-color-* constants typical of GnuCOBOL screen handling

purpose.domain_detail: Wordle-style word guessing game implemented in COBOL
purpose.summary: This program implements the core game loop for a Wordle-like word guessing game. It accepts a selected word and word list via linkage, displays a screen interface, accepts player guesses, validates them against the word list, and provides color-coded feedback (green for correct position, yellow for wrong position, black/white for not present). The game allows up to 6 tries to guess a 5-letter word.

notable_features: SCREEN SECTION with copybooks for screen definitions
LINKAGE SECTION with occurs clause referencing working-storage constant
SET ENVIRONMENT statements for GnuCOBOL screen control
INSPECT TALLYING for letter frequency counting
FUNCTION UPPER-CASE and FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC
Multiple CALL statements to helper subprograms (logger, display-info-text, update-remaining-letters, etc.)
verdict.notes: This is a COBOL implementation of a Wordle clone, authored by Erik Eriksen in April 2022. The code is well-structured with clear separation of concerns via subprogram calls. The duplicate SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph (appears twice) is a minor anomaly. The program is a subprogram called with USING, returning via GOBACK. Maturity is assessed as student-exercise/hobby project rather than production code.
